AMD Client segment PC CPU revenue market share 2026

findings.claim: Data Center segment revenue $6.7B in Q2 2026, up 107% YoY, driven by EPYC CPU and Instinct GPU sales
AMD guided Q3 2026 data center + embedded revenue to grow double-digit sequentially, and server CPU revenue to grow >80% YoY in H2 2026
findings.source: AMD Q2 2026 earnings slides via Investing.com https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/amd-q2-2026-slides-data-center-revenue-doubles-ai-partnerships-expand-93CH-4836256

findings.claim: AMD stated data center segment revenue should more than double in 2027, supported by ramp of Helios (MI400-series) platform
findings.source: AMD Q2 2026 earnings call/slides via Investing.com https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/amd-q2-2026-slides-data-center-revenue-doubles-ai-partnerships-expand-93CH-4836256

findings.claim: AMD data center revenue reached $5.8B in Q1 2026; company reiterated a long-term target of $120B server CPU-related revenue by 2030
AMD reached record 46.2% server x86 CPU revenue share in Q1 2026 (unit share ~30% of entire x86 CPU market)
NVIDIA holds an estimated 70-75% of data-center AI accelerator market revenue vs. AMD's estimated 6-8%; hyperscaler custom silicon collectively ~15-20%
AMD Instinct GPU line generated an estimated $7-8B in 2025 (~5-7% of AI accelerator revenue); MI400 series (CDNA5, 2nm, 432GB HBM4) launched July 2026 as first-to-market 2nm AI accelerator

Third-party analyst scenario projects AMD AI accelerator share could reach 15-20% by 2027 (vs. NVIDIA 75-80%), citing OpenAI 6GW compute commitment and Meta multi-year deals as catalysts; this is a market-analyst projection, not AMD guidance
AI data center GPU market projected to grow from $11.12B (2025) to $32.3B by 2030, a 23.8% CAGR
Client segment (PC CPU) unit market share reached 30.3% in Q2 2026 (first time above 30%), up from 29.6% in Q1 2026 and 24.1% a year earlier; Intel share fell to 69.7%
Client segment revenue was $3.1B in Q2 2026, up 23% YoY (from $2.5B); Q1 2026 client revenue was $2.9B, up 26% YoY, driven by Ryzen demand and share gains

Gaming segment revenue was $779M in Q2 2026, down 31% YoY, primarily due to lower semi-custom (console) revenue and higher component costs weighing on GPU demand at this late stage of the console cycle; AMD guided H2 2026 gaming revenue to be >20% lower than H1 2026

Gaming revenue was $720M in Q1 2026, up 11% YoY on higher Radeon GPU demand, partially offset by lower semi-custom revenue; customer demand for next-gen console platforms described as encouraging even as current-gen console sales decline late in the cycle

Embedded segment revenue was $977M in Q2 2026, up 19% YoY (strongest embedded growth in 3+ years), with operating margin at 40% (up from 33% a year earlier); segment tracking toward a record year with over $18B in new design wins, following a prolonged industrial inventory correction
Embedded segment revenue was $873M in Q1 2026, up 6% YoY, as industrial and edge demand began improving

end_markets.note: 涵蓋 AMD 四大營收段（Data Center／Client／Gaming／Embedded）逐段查證，另補 AI 加速器市佔與 TAM 作為 Data Center 段的關鍵子題。siliconanalysts.com 之市佔／2027 情境預測為第三方分析站推估，非 AMD 官方 guidance，已於 claim 內註明。
